positions.sentence: Instructors may decide whether and how generative AI is used in their own courses, from prohibiting it to encouraging it.
Instructors are responsible for setting and communicating their own course-level AI policy.
Instructors should decide, define and develop a clear AI policy suited to their course.
Policies state that the instructor or faculty member has the authority and discretion to decide AI use in a course.
Policies warn that AI rules differ across courses, instructors, disciplines and assignments, with no single approach.
Instructors may set different AI rules for different assignments within the same course.
Instructors should consider and provide assignment-level AI guidance rather than only a course-wide rule.
Instructors must state for each assignment whether AI use is allowed and how.
Instructors should state clearly to students whether and how AI may be used.
Policies state that assignments will specify whether and how AI tools may be used, and students will be informed.
Students may use generative AI only on assignments or in ways the instructor permits.
Students must follow the AI usage rules set for each assignment by the instructor or syllabus.
Students must not use AI in ways the instructor does not allow.
Universities should preserve faculty autonomy and avoid imposing one-size-fits-all AI rules.
Instructors may adopt or adapt the provided sample AI syllabus statements to fit their course.
Teaching assistants and consultants must follow the instructor's AI decisions and expectations.
Instructors may prohibit AI use entirely or strictly restrict it in their courses.
Policies leave decisions about misuse and consequences to the instructor's course policy.
The university sets no single AI policy and leaves decisions on AI use to faculty.
